sLabel.value: Shortage of people to carry on the work

oLabel.value: A significant decline in the working-age population

opText.value: It was explained that the decline in the working-age population is causing a shortage of workers.

tText.value: A particularly serious challenge is the sharp decline in the working-age population, those aged 15 to 64. In 1980, 43 years ago, there were about 84,600 working-age people; 20 years later, in 2000, there were about 75,500, a decrease of about 9,000 over two decades. By 2020, the figure had fallen to about 53,700, meaning that in the 20 years since the start of the 21st century, the working-age population declined by about 22,000. In a city of roughly 100,000 people, losing about 22,000 working-age residents in 20 years naturally leads to labor shortages in every field.

oLabel.value: A significant decline in the working-age population

opText.value: It is considered inevitable that a sharp decline in the working-age population will cause a shortage of people to carry on local industries

tText.value: A particularly serious challenge is the sharp decline in the working-age population, those aged 15 to 64. In 1980, 43 years ago, there were about 84,600 working-age people; 20 years later, in 2000, there were about 75,500, a decrease of about 9,000 over two decades. By 2020, the figure had fallen to about 53,700, meaning that in the 20 years since the start of the 21st century, the working-age population declined by about 22,000. In a city of roughly 100,000 people, losing about 22,000 working-age residents in 20 years naturally leads to labor shortages in every field.

sLabel.value: Construction defects at Sai Elementary School's gymnasium

oLabel.value: Insufficient concrete consolidation caused partial voids and aggregate segregation

stLabel.value: Ken Ishizuka, Director of the Education Department

opText.value: Construction conditions and equipment at the time were inadequate

tText.value: The construction defect we have referred to is what is known in construction terminology as honeycombing. Around 1963, concrete was mixed on-site and compacted by hand, and construction conditions and equipment were inadequate by today's standards. As a result, compaction was insufficient when concrete was poured into forms, creating partial voids through interference with reinforcing bars or steel frames and causing separation of cement and aggregate, which weakened the concrete.
